arxiv-2101-09253.title: Automatic Cerebral Vessel Extraction in TOF-MRA Using Deep Learning
arxiv-2101-09253.creator: V. de Vos, K.M. Timmins, I.C. van der Schaaf, Y. Ruigrok, B.K. Velthuis, H.J. Kuijf
arxiv-2101-09253.description: Abstract Deep learning approaches may help radiologists in the early diagnosis and timely treatment of cerebrovascular diseases. Accurate cerebral vessel segmentation of Time-of-Flight Magnetic Resonance Angiographs (TOF-MRAs) is an essential step in this process. This study investigates deep learning approaches for automatic, fast and accurate cerebrovascular segmentation for TOF-MRAs.

arxiv-2302-04417.title: Dynamic and Stochastic Rational Behavior Thanks: This paper subsumes “Nonparametric Analysis of Dynamic Random Utility Models.” The “ⓡ” symbol indicates that the authors’ names are in certified random order, as described by Ray and Robson 2018 . We thank Roy Allen, Chris Chambers, Pierre-André Chiap
arxiv-2302-04417.creator: Nail Kashaev ⓡ Victor H. Aguiar ⓡ Martin Plávala ⓡ Charles Gauthier
arxiv-2302-04417.description: Abstract The (static) utility maximization model of Afriat 1967 , which is the standard in analysing choice behavior, is under scrutiny. We propose the Dynamic Random Utility Model (DRUM) that is more flexible than the framework of Afriat 1967 and more informative than the static Random Utility Model (RUM) framework of McFadden and Richter 1990 .

arxiv-2407-05728.title: Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Stackelberg Differential Game with Asymmetric Informational Uncertainties: Robust Optimization Approach Thanks: This work is supported by National Key R&D Program of China (2022YFA1006104), National Natural Science Foundation of China (12271304), and Shandong Provincial N
arxiv-2407-05728.creator: Na Xiang, Jingtao Shi
arxiv-2407-05728.description: Abstract Abstract: This paper is concerned with a two-person zero-sum indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic Stackelberg differential game with asymmetric informational uncertainties, where both the leader and follower face different and unknown disturbances. We take a robust optimization approach and soft-constraint analysis, a min-max stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problem is solved by the follower firstly.

arxiv-2410-04536.title: Multi-LED Classification as Pretext For Robot Heading Estimation
arxiv-2410-04536.creator: Nicholas Carlotti, Mirko Nava, Alessandro Giusti
arxiv-2410-04536.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicholas Carlotti, Mirko Nava, Alessandro Giusti. We propose a self-supervised approach for visual robot detection and heading estimation by learning to estimate the states ( off or on ) of four independent robot-mounted LEDs. Experimental results show a median image-space position error of 14 14 px and relative heading MAE of 17 ​ ° , versus a supervised upperbound scoring 10 10 px and 8 ​ ° , respectively.

arxiv-2501-04096.title: Non-stop Variability of Sgr A* using JWST at 2.1 and 4.8 micron Wavelengths: Evidence for Distinct Populations of Faint and Bright Variable Emission
arxiv-2501-04096.creator: F. Yusef-Zadeh, H. Bushouse, R. G. Arendt, M. Wardle, J. M. Michail, C. J. Chandler
arxiv-2501-04096.description: Abstract We present first results of JWST Cycle 1 and 2 observations of Sgr A* using NIRCam taken simultaneously at 2.1 and 4.8 μ \mu m for a total of ∼ 48 \sim 48 h over seven different epochs in 2023 and 2024. We find correlated variability at 2.1 and 4.

arxiv-2502-10793.title: Dynamic Influence Tracker: Measuring Time-Varying Sample Influence During Training
arxiv-2502-10793.creator: Jie Xu, Zihan Wu
arxiv-2502-10793.description: Abstract Existing methods for measuring training sample influence on models only provide static, overall measurements, overlooking how sample influence changes during training. We propose Dynamic Influence Tracker (DIT), which captures the time-varying sample influence across arbitrary time windows during training.

arxiv-2506-05485.title: Theory of plasmon spectroscopy with the quantum twisting microscope
arxiv-2506-05485.creator: Nemin Wei, Francisco Guinea, Felix von Oppen, Leonid I. Glazman
arxiv-2506-05485.description: Abstract We consider plasmon-assisted electron tunneling in a quantum twisting microscope (QTM). The dependence of the differential conductance on the two control parameters of the QTM – the twist angle and bias – reveals the plasmon spectrum as well as the strength of plasmon-electron interactions in the sample.

arxiv-2511-11941.title: Error-Mitigation Enabled Multicomponent Quantum Simulations Beyond the Born–Oppenheimer Approximation
arxiv-2511-11941.creator: Delmar G. A. Cabral, Brandon Allen, Fabijan Pavošević, Sharon Hammes-Schiffer, Pablo Díez-Valle, Jack S. Baker, Gaurav Saxena, Thi Ha Kyaw, Victor S. Batista
arxiv-2511-11941.description: Abstract We introduce a multicomponent unitary coupled cluster framework for quantum simulations of molecular systems that incorporate both electronic and nuclear quantum effects beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation. Using the nuclear–electronic orbital formalism, we construct mcUCC ansätze for positronium hydride and molecular hydrogen with a quantum proton, and analyze hardware requirements for different excitation truncations.

arxiv-2602-22513.title: Nonlinear stabilization of chiral modes in space-time modulated parametric oscillators
arxiv-2602-22513.creator: Scott Lambert, Elise Jaremko, Jayson Paulose
arxiv-2602-22513.description: Abstract Phase control of parametric modulation in coupled oscillator networks enables sculpting of dynamical states with desired spatiotemporal symmetries. Symmetry-aware Floquet analysis successfully predicts such states in linear systems, but whether their symmetry properties persist under nonlinearity remains largely unexplored.

pmc-11331913.title: Does regional implementation of a clinical pathway for older adult patients with pelvic fragility fractures after low-energy trauma improve patient outcomes (PELVIC): a multicentre, stepped-wedge, randomised controlled trial
pmc-11331913.creator: Anna H M Mennen, Marte Lommerse, Robert Hemke, Hanna C Willems, Mario Maas, Frank W Bloemers, Kees Jan Ponsen, Daphne Van Embden
pmc-11331913.description: IntroductionPatients with pelvic fragility fractures suffer from high morbidity and mortality rates. Despite the high incidence, there is currently no regional or nationwide treatment protocol which results in a wide variety of clinical practices. Recently, there have been new insights into treatment strategies, such as early diagnosis and minimally invasive operative treatment.

pmc-11350769.title: Isolation of Aerobic Bacterial Species Associated with Palpable Udder Defects in Non-Dairy Ewes
pmc-11350769.creator: Mandefrot M Zeleke, Paul R Kenyon, Kate J Flay, Danielle Aberdein, Sarah J Pain, Niluka Velathanthiri, Anne L Ridler, Alfonso Zecconi
pmc-11350769.description: Simple SummaryMilk or mammary tissue swab samples were collected from both defective and normal udder halves in three different studies to identify the bacterial species involved. Samples were collected at different physiological time points: pre-mating, throughout lactation, at weaning and post-weaning. Numerous bacterial species were identified, with Staphylococcus species, Mannheimia haemolytica and Streptococcus being the most frequently isolated.

pmc-11604525.title: Integrative single-cell multi-omics of CD19-CARpos and CARneg T cells suggest drivers of immunotherapy response in B cell neoplasias
pmc-11604525.creator: Mercedes Guerrero-Murillo, Aina Rill-Hinarejos, Juan L Trincado, Alex Bataller, Valentín Ortiz-Maldonado, Daniel Benítez-Ribas, Marta Español-Rego, E Azucena González-Navarro, Nuria Martínez-Cibrián, Doménica Marchese, Lourdes Martín-Martín, Alejandro Martín García-Sancho, Susana Rives, Holger Heyn,
pmc-11604525.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryThe impact of phenotypic, clonal, and functional heterogeneity of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells on clinical outcome remains understudied. Here, we integrate clonal kinetics with transcriptomic heterogeneity resolved by single-cell omics to interrogate cellular dynamics of non-transduced (CARneg) and transduced (CARpos) T cells, in the infusion product (IP) and at the CAR-T cell expansion peak in five B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) patients treated with CD19CAR-T cells (varni-cel). We identify significant differences in cellular dynamics in response to therapy.

pmc-11660260.title: Adverse Tissue Reaction to Metal and Polyethylene Particles as the Major Underlying Pathogenesis in Revision Total Ankle Arthroplasty
pmc-11660260.creator: Jensen Henry, Yaxia Zhang, Emily Teehan, Thomas W Bauer, Constantine Demetracopoulos
pmc-11660260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Category:Ankle Arthritis; Basic Sciences/BiologicsIntroduction/Purpose:Recent advancements in prosthesis design and surgical techniques have improved the clinical outcomes of total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) for end-stage ankle arthritis, leading to pain relief and better function. However, some patients experience complications such as impingement, peri-implant cysts and osteolysis, and implant subsidence and loosening, ultimately necessitating reoperation or revision TAA (exchange or removal of one or both metal components).

pmc-12398995.title: Combined lifestyle habits, subjective well-being, and all-cause mortality among older adults in China
pmc-12398995.creator: Chunsu Zhu, Zhiwei Lian, Jing Sun, Yongying Huang, Shengmei Li, Heng Zhang, Jianmin Wang
pmc-12398995.description: BackgroundAlthough studies have demonstrated that both lifestyles and subjective well-being (SWB) are associated with mortality risk, the joint effects of a healthy lifestyle and SWB on the risk of mortality are unclear. This study aimed to explore the combined impact of lifestyles and SWB on total mortality among the older Chinese population.

pmc-12534366.title: Pólya-Szegő Inequalities on Submanifolds with Small Total Mean Curvature
pmc-12534366.creator: Pietro Aldrigo, Zoltán M Balogh
pmc-12534366.description: We establish Pólya-Szegő-type inequalities (PSIs) for Sobolev-functions defined on a regular n-dimensional submanifold Σ (possibly with boundary) of a (n+m)-dimensional Euclidean space, under explicit upper bounds of the total mean curvature. The p-Sobolev and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities, as well as the spectral gap in W01,p(Σ) are derived as corollaries.

pmc-12730355.title: Complete Mitochondrial Genomes of Spotted Forest Musk Deer (Moschus berezovskii) from Huanglong Mountain, Shaanxi, China, and Phylogenetic Analysis of Moschidae
pmc-12730355.creator: Kuo Sun, Xiao Tan, Lei Zhang, Ying Dai, Kun Bian, Feiran Li, Lijuan Suo, Xiaojuan Du, Chao Yang, Jie Tang
pmc-12730355.description: Simple SummaryMusk deer are small, shy animals that live in the mountains and forests of East Asia. They are famous for producing musk, a valuable substance used in traditional medicine and perfumes. However, the number of wild musk deer has dropped sharply due to illegal hunting and habitat loss.

pmc-13219446.title: Generation of single-mode and two-mode quantum squeezed states of light by degenerate four-wave mixing in a plasmonic waveguide
pmc-13219446.creator: Abbas Ghasempour Ardakani, Hossein Bornak
pmc-13219446.description: Squeezed states of light represent one of the most fundamental concepts in quantum optics. They play a crucial role in various fields of science, quantum technology, and photonics, with applications in quantum information processing, quantum computation, quantum sensing, and gravitational wave detection. In this paper, we propose a plasmonic waveguide for the generation of squeezed states via four-wave mixing.

pmc-13247351.title: Hybrid Calcium Hydroxylapatite–Polynucleotide Skin Booster A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13247351.creator: Andrea Lazzarotto, Stefania Guida, Jonathan Kadouch, Nabil Fakih‐Gomez, Nicola Zerbinati, Luigi Colombo, Massimo Vitale, Mariana César Corrêa, Kyu‐Ho Yi
pmc-13247351.description: BackgroundSkin quality is increasingly recognized as a multidimensional construct that includes tone evenness, surface evenness, firmness, and radiance. Injectable ‘skin boosters’ have expanded treatment options for diffuse skin‐quality concerns, and combinations of biostimulatory and regenerative agents are increasingly used in practice.

pmc-13389013.title: Possible high-temperature superconductivity in LiCuH at ambient pressure
pmc-13389013.creator: Prutthipong Tsuppayakorn-aek, Sirinee Thasitha, Anan Udomkijmongkol, Wiwittawin Sukmas, Tanveer Hussain, Thiti Bovornratanaraks, Komsilp Kotmool
pmc-13389013.description: We theoretically investigate the structural stability, electronic property, and superconductivity of the hydrogen-rich compound LiCuH in its face-centered cubic phase. First-principles calculations show that LiCuH is thermodynamically metastable at ambient pressure but dynamically stable. Moreover, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulation at 300 K further confirms that LiCuH remains structurally intact without decomposition.

pmc-13543981.title: Adaptive and degenerative mitochondrial remodeling define distinct redox states in age-related macular degeneration
pmc-13543981.creator: Cecilia Giulivi, Carol Villafuerte-Trisolini, Zoe Lee Greenblatt, Jennifer Dang, Atena Tork, Rida Mullah, Sophie Le, Angela Min, Maya Nair, Aldo Vorkapich, Huy-An Tran, Elizabeth Doyle, Alestor Law, Owen O'Keefe, Annabelle Wu, Bradley Shibata, Ana Ripolles-Garcia, Sara M Thomasy, R Alan Harris, Rui
pmc-13543981.description: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, yet the relationship between mitochondrial remodeling, redox homeostasis, and disease progression remains poorly understood. Nonhuman primates (NHPs) develop spontaneous AMD-related phenotypes, including punctate deposits and soft drusen, providing a unique animal model to investigate mitochondrial pathology in the aging retinal pigment epithelium (RPE).
